bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 50433 (c-blosc2): AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 in `_sw32`, reachable from `compress_frame_fuzzer`.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 2-byte file `5b 21`. In `compress_frame_fuzzer`, `size == 2` makes the only append call use `chunksize == 2`, and byte `0x5b` sets `cparams.clevel = data[0] % 10 = 1`, so the compression context is not pre-marked as memcpy-only. `blosc2_schunk_append_buffer()` allocates `nbytes + BLOSC2_MAX_OVERHEAD = 34` bytes for the compressed chunk. `initialize_context_compression()` then materializes `sourcesize = 2`, `destsize = 34`, and `clevel = 1` in the active context. `blosc_stune_next_blocksize()` clamps `blocksize` to `2`, and `blosc2_calculate_blocks()` therefore derives `nblocks = 1`. Vulnerable `write_compression_header()` always runs in extended-header mode here, so it sets `header_overhead = 32`; because the vulnerable code only sets `BLOSC_MEMCPYED` when `clevel == 0` and lacks the patch's missing `context->sourcesize < BLOSC_MIN_BUFFERSIZE` guard, `memcpyed` stays false for this 2-byte input. The function therefore lays out `bstarts = dest + 32` and `output_bytes = 32 + 4 * 1 = 36` inside the 34-byte heap buffer. `blosc_compress_context()` enters `do_job()` before any memcpy fallback, `do_job()` takes the serial path, and the first `serial_blosc()` iteration executes `_sw32(bstarts + 0, ntbytes)` with `ntbytes == 36`. `_sw32` writes a 4-byte integer at `dest + 32`, which spans bytes 32-35 of a 34-byte allocation and overruns the heap buffer by 2 bytes. AddressSanitizer reports the saved `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4` at `blosc-private.h:128`. The patch fixes the missing obligation by re-adding the small-buffer memcpy check before the `bstarts` table is created, and it adds a regression test for tiny inputs.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-derived size into the heap buffer that is later overrun by the header's `bstarts` table.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` at `gt_results/arvo_50433/poc` is exactly 2 bytes: `5b 21`. In `tests/fuzz/fuzz_compress_frame.c`, the only loop iteration reduces `chunksize` to `size - i = 2` before calling `blosc2_schunk_append_buffer`, so `nbytes == 2` here and the allocation size becomes `2 + BLOSC2_MAX_OVERHEAD = 34`. Earlier in the same fuzz iteration, byte `0x5b` made `cparams.clevel = data[0] % 10 = 1`, so the `schunk->cctx` used by this append call will later keep `write_compression_header()` out of the `clevel == 0` memcpy path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-derived destination extent (`34`), source size (`2`), and previously configured compression level (`1`) become the active compression-context state consumed by block tuning, header layout, and the later non-memcpy decision.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the saved witness, `dest` points to the 34-byte heap allocation from step 1, `srcsize == 2`, `destsize == 34`, and `clevel == 1` because the fuzzer created `schunk->cctx` from `cparams.clevel = 0x5b % 10` before the append call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The 4-byte little-endian store writes the first block-start offset into `chunk + 32` even though the heap allocation is only 34 bytes long.
sink.note: In the saved ASan run, `dest_ == chunk + 32` and `a == 36`, so this store spans bytes 32-35 of the 34-byte region `[chunk, chunk + 34)`. The sanitizer reports `WRITE of size 4` at `blosc/blosc-private.h:128:23` with stack `_sw32 -> serial_blosc -> do_job`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The vulnerable header builder only marks the chunk as memcpy-only when `clevel == 0`; it omits the patch's missing `context->sourcesize < BLOSC_MIN_BUFFERSIZE` check, so the witnessed 2-byte buffer is handled as a normal compressed chunk and later gets a `bstarts` table that does not fit.
root_cause.note: For this witness `clevel == 1` and `sourcesize == 2`, so `memcpyed` remains false even though the input is far below the small-buffer threshold. The fix inserts `if (context->sourcesize < BLOSC_MIN_BUFFERSIZE) { context->header_flags |= (uint8_t)BLOSC_MEMCPYED; }` at this point.

parser_admitted.description: For the 2-byte witness the fuzz loop executes exactly once, reduces `chunksize` to `2`, and enters project compression through `blosc2_schunk_append_buffer`. The same iteration already set `cparams.clevel = 1` from byte `0x5b`, and the saved ASan stack confirms the crash descends from this append call.

fine_trace.note: Source. The staged witness is exactly 2 bytes, so the only fuzz-loop iteration calls this function with `nbytes == 2` and allocates a 34-byte heap buffer for the compressed chunk. The same fuzz iteration already configured `schunk->cctx->clevel = 1` from byte `0x5b`, so later header construction will not take the `clevel == 0` memcpy shortcut.

The append call's heap buffer and length become active compression state: `context->dest` points to the 34-byte allocation from step 1, `context->destsize == 34`, `context->sourcesize == 2`, and `context->clevel == 1` is copied from the previously configured compression context.

Automatic tuning keeps tiny buffers unsplit: this function starts with `blocksize = nbytes`, and with `nbytes == 2`, `typesize == 1`, and no user-forced blocksize, the final tuned `context->blocksize` remains `2`.
With `sourcesize == 2` and `blocksize == 2`, the compressor derives exactly one block and no leftover bytes: `nblocks == 1`, `leftover == 0`.

Root cause. The witnessed context has `clevel == 1`, so this check leaves `BLOSC_MEMCPYED` clear. Because the vulnerable source lacks the patch's `if (context->sourcesize < BLOSC_MIN_BUFFERSIZE)` guard, `memcpyed` stays false even though `sourcesize == 2` is a tiny buffer that should have bypassed the `bstarts` table.

`blosc2_compress_ctx()` always calls this helper with `extended_header == true`, so the header overhead is 32 bytes. With default `use_dict == 0`, `dict_training` is false; because step 5 left `memcpyed` false, this branch takes the `else` arm and places `bstarts` at `chunk + 32` while setting `output_bytes = 32 + 4 * 1 = 36`.

Because step 5 left `memcpyed` false, compression enters `do_job()` immediately. The later memcpy fallback and its `sourcesize + header_overhead > destsize` size check are not reached before the overflowing write happens.
The crash takes the serial compressor path. The witness satisfies the second half of the predicate exactly (`2 / 2 == 1`), so `do_job()` dispatches into `serial_blosc()` for the single derived block.

On the first and only loop iteration, `j == 0`, `bstarts == chunk + 32`, and `ntbytes` starts from `context->output_bytes == 36`. Because this is compression, `memcpyed` is false, and default `dict_training` is false, the code immediately emits the first 4-byte block-start offset to `chunk + 32`.

Sink. The saved run is little-endian, so `_sw32` performs a 4-byte store at `dest_ == chunk + 32` with `a == 36`. That write covers bytes 32-35 of a 34-byte heap allocation and therefore overruns the buffer by 2 bytes, exactly matching AddressSanitizer's `WRITE of size 4` report.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_50433-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged 2-byte `poc` to `compress_frame_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4` in `_sw32` with stack `_sw32 -> serial_blosc -> do_job`.

format.name: raw bytes
format.contract: Exact 2-byte witness `5b 21`. In the saved run `size == 2` makes the only append call use `nbytes == 2`, and byte `0x5b` makes `cparams.clevel = 1`, so `write_compression_header()` stays on the non-memcpy extended-header path that creates `bstarts` inside a 34-byte chunk buffer.
